summary: Rudolf Much was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna from circa 1882 to 1887 and later held a post there from circa 1892 to 1934.

Working in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, Rudolf Otto studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1888-1890) and under Richard von Garbe. He held posts at the University of Breslau (~1914-1917) and the University of Marburg (~1917-1929).

Rudolf Seydel worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1852 to 1856 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1860 to 1892.

Linguist Rudolf Thurneysen studied at the University of Leipzig (~1876-1879) and under Heinrich Zimmer (~1878-1880). He held posts at the University of Jena (~1882-1887), University of Freiburg (~1887-1913), and University of Bonn (~1913-1923).

Rudolf von Roth worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tübinger Stift (~1839-1843) under Heinrich Ewald and under Eugène Burnouf (~1843-1844), later holding posts at the University of Tübingen from 1845 and 1848 to 1895.

Working in Indology and history/archaeology, Rudrapatna Shamasastry studied at Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, University of Madras, Oriental University, and University of Calcutta. He was Principal at Sri Chamarajendra Samskrita Maha Patashala (1912-1918), Curator at ORI Mysore (1918-1929), and Director of the Mysore Archaeological Department (1926).

Ruixuan Chen specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Chen studied at Leiden University and under Jens-Uwe Hartmann, Adelheid Mette, Olav Hackstein, Paul Harrison, and Helmut Tauscher, and is attested as Peking University faculty in 2026.

Rulon Wells worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (~1935-1939) and Harvard University (~1939-1942), later holding a post at Yale University from circa 1945 to 1989.

Buddhist studies and Indology scholar Rupert Gethin earned a BA and PhD at the University of Manchester, studying under Lance S. Cousins. His career includes posts at the University of Bristol (Lecturer 1987; Co-Director 2009-2023) and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Nagoya University. Her career includes posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Active in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Ruth Fuller Sasaki studied at the University of Chicago and under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki, Zuigan Goto, and Mukai Kono. She was director of the First Zen Institute of America (~1945-1967) and abbess of Ryōsen-an (~1958-1967).

Ruth Gamble works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the Australian National University under supervisors John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman, later holding posts at ANU and the University of Munich.

Ruth W. Dunnell works in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD from Princeton University in 1983, studied under Jinbo Shi, and served as James P. Storer Associate Professor of Asian History at Kenyon College.

Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under doctoral supervisor Jason Neelis (attested 2017).

Ryan Matthew Jacobson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Naropa University, earning an MA in Religious Studies, and was taught by several teachers including Judith Simmer-Brown, David Phillip Stanley, Sarah Harding, Tsultrim Allione, and Gochen Tulku Sang-ngag Rinpoche.

Ryan Richard Overbey works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Brown University and Harvard University, and has held posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, College of the Holy Cross, UC Berkeley (2013-2015), and Wesleyan University.
Ryo Kuroiwa works in computational fields and Indology. Kuroiwa has held posts at the National Institute of Informatics and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.
Ryo Nishimura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University from circa 1991 to 2001 and was taught by Fumihiko Sueki from circa 1996 to 2004.
Ryodo Kudo is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Kudo's academic career includes posts at Taisho University (attested 2015-2026) and Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Humboldt University of Berlin under Shun'ichi Takagi, Ryujo Yamada, and Ryotai Hatani. He later held posts lecturing at Humboldt University and as professor at Ryukoku University.
